positions.title: Chief Software Engineer
positions.description:
Responsible for all software development and software certification activities for all Astronics Advanced Electronic Systems. Reviewed and guided all software development for Astronics.

	Performed systems engineering function and designed software architecture for an airborne controller of an Electrical Power Distribution System for a new business jet. This is a DO-178B Level A system designed to control and monitor electronic circuit breakers for all aircraft systems.

	Performed systems engineering and project management for an Electronic Flight Information System (EFIS) Control Panel for the 737 Next Generation

positions.title: Manager, Software Engineering
positions.description:
Managed all software development activities for all Astronics Avionics systems installed in Commercial Passenger Aircraft.  Led company initiative to define software processes that aligned with DO-178B requirements and to move the Company's Software Capability level from CMMI Level 1 to CMMI Level 3. 

	Led team to create a series of Intelligent In-Seat Power Supplies for various IFE vendors and airline customers.

positions.title: Software Team Leader
positions.description:
Led a team of engineers to design and implement the software for the EmPort Airborne Network. This system allows passengers on Commercial Airlines to plug their laptop computers into an in-seat USB port in order to send/receive e-mail and surf the internet. Over the previous 3 years prior to my arrival, the software group had made numerous starts and resets with no resulting progress. I organized the team, wrote the software requirements, designed the software architecture to fit within the framework of the existing hardware, and implemented configuration control and design procedures. The system was certified in July of 2001 and was subsequently deployed in August 2001, on schedule. 

Developed a Power Management Control Unit (MCU) to distribute power in Commercial Jet's Passenger Cabin. This system distributed limited aircraft power across 5 columns, monitored the column loads, limited loads to avoid overload conditions, and used relays to act as an electronic circuit breaker. The system communicated with other avionics equipment via Ethernet using SNMP protocol. I developed the software requirements, worked with Airbus to define the Ethernet Interface, designed the software architecture, and designed and implemented the main control and power management functions.
 
Designed the software architecture for an In-Flight Entertainment system. This system would place a tablet PC in the back of each seat with storage for multiple audio and visual entertainment options enabling audio and video on demand. 

Designed the software architecture for Portable Media Player and ground loading station for a In-Flight Entertainment system.  The loading station would automatically download usage data and upload new content and software updates via a USB interface. 

Managed all software planning and certification activities for these projects. All certification was to RTCA DO-178B standards.

positions.title: Instructor
positions.description: Taught Visual Basic and Windows programming.

positions.title: Senior Project Engineer
positions.description: Led a team of 8 engineers to design and implement the software for the LifePak 500 Automated External Defibrillator.  The LifePak 500 is a heart monitor/defibrillator designed for layman use.  It automatically analyzes a patients heart rhythm, determines the correct energy for therapy, then delivers an electric shock to restart the patients heart. Designed the system architecture and implemented the major control functions.  Supervised and approved the design of all the LifePak 500 subsystems.  Added increased functionality to the LifePak 500 as requested by customers.  Added software to control a new Biphasic waveform, implemented an Asystole Detector function, and added the capability to record episode data and upload the data to a PC for review by medical doctors.  Worked on team to design the system architecture for LifePak 20 full-featured defibrillator.

positions.title: Software Design Engineer
positions.description: Designed and implemented the 777 Cabin Management System (CMS) Data Load function to load operational software and databases into Boeing 777 CMS avionics.  Led small team to implement the data load function in C on a duel Intel processor running UNIX and MS Windows.  Used multi-threading to reduce load time by up to 80% over the previous implementation of the application; thus, enabling the airlines to achieve gate turn around goals.  Received several awards for implementing a defect free application.

positions.title: Software/Systems Engineer
positions.description: Used Visual Basic and the Access database to prototype an order entry system for Krell products. Used structured analysis to create the system specification for the BE Aerospace BE-4000 Inflight Entertainment System.  Designed the KRELL- 1000 Cabin Terminal System, an Intel based avionics system that provides wireless data communications to the ground via the ACARS system.

positions.title: Systems Engineer
positions.description: Founded Krell Software, a software consulting firm. Provided System Engineering consulting services to Boeing for the 777 Cabin Management System.  Performed Functional Analysis for the OSI, ARINC 629 and ARINC 429 network protocols.  Used Object Oriented Design and the Ada programming language to implement these protocols on Motorola 68XXX processors.

positions.title: Engineering Manager
positions.description: Promoted to Engineering Manager of Sundstrand's ACARS (Aircraft Communications Addressing and Reporting System) wireless data communications products.  Supervised 20 engineers.  Managed the design and implementation of all applications for new and existing airline customers.  Negotiated with customers to define their applications and set the product price.  Provided engineering support to marketing at sales presentations.  Represented Sundstrand at industry meetings to define the Open Systems Interconnect (OSI) protocols used by the Aeronautical Telecommunications Network (ATN

positions.title: Research Specialist
positions.description: Chief Architect of hardware/software redesign of Sundstrand's ARINC 724B ACARS, an Intel 80x86 based embedded real-time avionics system for wireless data communications.  Used structured analysis to redesign the system architecture to meet airline and FAA DO-178 requirements.  Used structured design and multi-threading to implement the ARINC 429 protocol handlers for communication with the Flight Deck Display (MCDU ARINC 739), the Flight Deck Printer (ARINC 740), and other aircraft avionics.  Used Object-Oriented Design (OOD) to implement the Microsoft Windows ground support software used to reprogram the airborne system.

positions.title: Lead Software Design Engineer
positions.description: Supervised the Software Group for a Boeing Proprietary Project.  Designed a real-time telemetry processing tool and an interactive simulation to compare predicted vehicle flight characteristics with actual test data.  These systems subsequently passed System Validation Testing without a single reported defect.  Received Pride in Excellence Award for implementing a Zero-Defect Product.  Designed the Man/Machine Interface for a real-time simulation and the data analysis software.   Named 1987 Project Employee of the Year for bringing the project's Systems Integration Laboratory test system on-line in 25% of the expected time. Each year I planned and successfully obtained from Boeing Corporate the project's annual capital equipment budget (approximately $10 million annually

positions.title: Software Design Engineer
positions.description: Used structured analysis to design a "Hardware In The Loop" real-time simulation for a Boeing Proprietary Project.  Specific areas of responsibility included analysis and design of the Navigation and Engine simulation models; and design and implementation of the Aerodynamic and Mass models.  All models were written in FORTRAN and assembler and ran on a Floating Point Systems Array Processor hosted on a Gould MPX/32 computer.

positions.title: Software Design Engineer
positions.description: Designed and implemented the Software Configuration Management System for a Boeing Proprietary Project.

positions.title: Software Test Engineer
positions.description: Wrote test procedures and conducted tests of avionics software for the B-1B bomber using Mil-Std-1750 computers and Mil-Std-1553 protocols.

positions.title: Computer Programmer/Operator
positions.description: Supervised student computer laboratories.  Assisted students with their programming assignments.

positions.title: Computer Programmer/Operator
positions.description: Wrote COBOL programs to run payroll and accounting systems for clients.
